ops.name: anim.bake_follow
ops.summary: Make a follower animation (a MetaHuman face's) carry its leader's pose: bake_pose from the leader (the body)
ops.doc:
Make a follower animation (a MetaHuman face's) carry its leader's pose: bake_pose from the leader (the body)
into `out` for every non-facial bone the two skeletons share, and switch the face rig's own head control off
(headcontrolswitch 0) unless `head_control`, so the head turns only as the body's does. A face playing alone
otherwise keeps its neck and chest apart from the body, and its chest pokes through the clothes. Multi-tick.

ops.name: anim.bake_pose
ops.summary: Sample `source` (a skeletal mesh component of the actor) as it really plays in `sequence` (animation, rig and
ops.doc:
Sample `source` (a skeletal mesh component of the actor) as it really plays in `sequence` (animation, rig and
post-process correctives included) and write those bones, local to their parents, as bone tracks into `out` (a
copy of `anim`), which then goes on `target`'s track. Keys past the sequence keep the animation's own pose; curves
are untouched. A multi-tick job.

ops.name: anim.gaze_lock
ops.summary: Keep a talking face's eyes on the lens, measured rather than guessed: `out` (a copy of `anim`) goes on
ops.doc:
Keep a talking face's eyes on the lens, measured rather than guessed: `out` (a copy of `anim`) goes on
`component`'s track in `sequence` (on the sections that play `anim`, wherever they start); the eye-look curves are
calibrated on the rig, then solved per frame from the eye bones' real pose (head and body motion included)
toward `camera`, with small saccades, and refined `iterations` times against a fresh measurement.
`target` aims the eyes elsewhere: a point [x, y, z], an actor (+ `target_offset` in its frame) or
"Label:Component:bone" (her eyes: "Presenter:Face:FACIAL_L_Eye"); with `frames` [first, last] only in that range
(the camera, if given, elsewhere). Frames with neither keep the animation's own eye curves. Returns the angle error
per pass. A multi-tick job.

ops.name: anim.head_to_body
ops.summary: Give the body the head motion a face rig makes from speech (HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll spread down the neck): bake the
ops.doc:
Give the body the head motion a face rig makes from speech (HeadYaw/Pitch/Roll spread down the neck): bake the
face's spine, neck and head as they play into `out` (a copy of the body's animation), which goes on the body's
track. Then bake_follow puts the whole shared skeleton back on the face, so both move as one. Multi-tick.

ops.name: assets.audit
ops.summary: What in a folder needs attention: assets nothing uses (and no level), redirectors, materials that do not
ops.doc:
What in a folder needs attention: assets nothing uses (and no level), redirectors, materials that do not
compile (they draw the engine's checker), material instances whose textures do not match their samplers.

Args: folder: content folder (recursive). unused: report unused assets. broken: compile-check materials (loads
      them: slower). limit: at most this many of each.
Returns: {"pass", "issues": [{"code": asset.unused | asset.redirector | material.not_compiling |
         material.texture_kind, "severity", "subject", "message", "fix"}], "metrics": {"assets", "unused",
         "redirectors", "broken"}}.
Example: film-ue op assets.audit folder=/Game/Props

ops.name: assets.catalog
ops.summary: The assets of a folder as data, from the asset registry (no loading): path, class, size in cm, triangles,
ops.doc:
The assets of a folder as data, from the asset registry (no loading): path, class, size in cm, triangles,
LODs, Nanite, material count, texture size/format, source file. Cached in Saved/fmbridge/catalog.json.

Args: folder: content folder (recursive). cls: one class (StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture2D, Material,
      MaterialInstanceConstant, Blueprint, SoundWave, AnimSequence, GroomAsset, ...). refresh: rebuild now.
      load: also load meshes whose counts are missing, and read metadata tags (slower). max_age_s: reuse a
      cached catalog this young. limit: at most this many entries returned.
Returns: {"folder", "count", "built_at", "entries": [{"path", "name", "class", "size_cm": [x, y, z],
         "triangles", "lods", "nanite", "materials", "dimensions", "format", "source", "tags"}]}.
Example: film-ue op assets.catalog folder=/Game/Props cls=StaticMesh

ops.name: assets.delete
ops.summary: Delete an asset now, used or not (prefer assets.remove, which checks who uses it first); False if absent.
ops.doc:
Delete an asset now, used or not (prefer assets.remove, which checks who uses it first); False if absent.
Example: film-ue assets delete --path /Game/Old/SM_Box

ops.name: assets.describe
ops.summary: One asset as numbers: class, size in cm and bounds, triangles/vertices per LOD, Nanite, collision, material
ops.doc:
One asset as numbers: class, size in cm and bounds, triangles/vertices per LOD, Nanite, collision, material
slots (meshes); size, sRGB, compression, LOD group (textures); parent and parameters (materials: see

Args: path: /Game/... asset. refs: include referencers/dependencies.
Returns: {"path", "class", ...per class..., "source", "tags", "referencers", "dependencies"}.

ops.name: assets.duplicate
ops.summary: Copy an asset (a MetaHuman preset, a material...) to a new path; an existing `dst` is kept unless overwrite
ops.doc:
Copy an asset (a MetaHuman preset, a material...) to a new path; an existing `dst` is kept unless overwrite

Example: film-ue assets duplicate --src /Game/M/MI_A --dst /Game/M/MI_B

ops.name: assets.find
ops.summary: Search assets by what they are and how big: words (name, folders, tags; a few synonyms: sofa/couch...), a
ops.doc:
Search assets by what they are and how big: words (name, folders, tags; a few synonyms: sofa/couch...), a
size ("a 45 cm chair", "table 120x80 cm", "lamp 1.5 m tall"), class, a name glob, tags, size bounds. Each hit
says how far its size is from the asked one and the uniform scale that would make it exact.

Args: query: plain words with optional sizes (mm/cm/m/in/ft; no unit = cm; tall/wide/long pick the axis).
      cls: StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture2D, MaterialInstanceConstant, ... folder: where to look.
      name: a glob on the asset name (SM_Chair*). tags: {key: value} metadata tags (assets.tag) to match.
      min_size_cm / max_size_cm: [x, y, z] bounds the size must be within (0 = no bound on that axis).
      limit: at most this many. refresh: rebuild the catalog first.
Returns: {"query": parsed, "hits": [{"path", "class", "size_cm", "score" 0..1, "size_error", "scale", ...}],
         "count"}. Nothing found: hits [] and a hint.
Example: film-ue op assets.find 'query=a 45 cm chair' cls=StaticMesh

ops.name: assets.fix_redirectors
ops.summary: Repoint everything that references a redirector (left behind by a rename/move) at the real asset and delete
ops.doc:
Repoint everything that references a redirector (left behind by a rename/move) at the real asset and delete
the redirectors, without a dialog.

Args: folder: where to look (recursive).
Returns: {"fixed": int, "left": [redirectors that could not be fixed], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.fix_redirectors folder=/Game/Props

ops.name: assets.folder
ops.summary: Content folders: make one, rename/move one (with everything in it), or remove an empty one.
ops.doc:
Content folders: make one, rename/move one (with everything in it), or remove an empty one.

Args: path: /Game/... folder. action: make | rename | remove. to: the new folder path for rename.
Returns: {"path", "changed", "to"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.folder path=/Game/Props/Chairs

ops.name: assets.import
ops.summary: Import files on the box into a content folder, any format, with no dialog: FBX/OBJ/glTF/GLB (Interchange),
ops.doc:
Import files on the box into a content folder, any format, with no dialog: FBX/OBJ/glTF/GLB (Interchange),
Alembic (static, geometry cache, skeletal, or a groom), USD, images (settings by role, see
assets.import_textures), WAV. Returns the new assets' object paths (or with detail, per file).

Args: files: paths on the box. dest: content folder. replace: re-import over existing (an Interchange re-import);
      false keeps what an earlier import of the same file made in dest (changed false).
      combine: merge an FBX's parts into one static mesh. kind: static | skeletal | auto (what the file says) |
      geometry_cache (Alembic). skeleton: /Game/... Skeleton for skeletal meshes/animations (else a new one).
      scale: uniform import scale (the source's units are converted to cm first). nanite: build Nanite (default
      on for static). collision: none | box | sphere | capsule | convex | convex10 | convex26 (a simple shape
      generated). lods: import LODs in the file. materials/textures: import the file's materials and textures.
      animations: import animations. groom: an Alembic of hair curves -> a Groom asset. abc_preset: maya | max |
      none (Alembic axis conversion). name: asset name for a single file. detail: return
      {"imported": [{"file", "kind", "assets", "objects"}], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.import 'files=["/data/props/chair.fbx"]' dest=/Game/Props/Chair collision=convex

ops.name: assets.import_textures
ops.summary: Import image files as textures with the right settings for what each is: the role from its name
ops.doc:
Import image files as textures with the right settings for what each is: the role from its name
(T_Rock_BaseColor, _Normal, _ORM, _Roughness, _AO, ... see assets.md), a PNG named nothing useful but that looks
like a normal map is one, else colour.

Args: files: images on the box. folder: every image in a box folder. dest: content folder. role: force one
      role for all. replace: import again over existing textures (else kept).
Returns: {"textures": [{"file", "path", "role", "imported"}], "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.import_textures folder=/data/tex/rock dest=/Game/Rock/Textures

ops.name: assets.list
ops.summary: Assets under a path, optionally of one class name ('StaticMesh', 'MetaHumanCharacter', ...): [class, path].
ops.doc:
Assets under a path, optionally of one class name ('StaticMesh', 'MetaHumanCharacter', ...): [class, path].

ops.name: assets.mesh
ops.summary: Converge a static mesh's build settings: Nanite, generated LODs, simple collision, lightmap UVs, CPU access.
ops.doc:
Converge a static mesh's build settings: Nanite, generated LODs, simple collision, lightmap UVs, CPU access.

Args: path: /Game/... StaticMesh. nanite: on/off. nanite_keep_percent: 0..100 triangles kept by Nanite.
      lods: number of LODs to generate (1 = just the base; generated by reduction: LOD i keeps lod_percents[i] %
      of the triangles, default 100, 50, 25, 12.5...). collision: none (remove simple collision) | box | sphere |
      capsule | convex (a decomposition into convex_hulls hulls) | ndop10 | ndop18 | ndop26. lightmap_uv:
      generate lightmap UVs. cpu_access: allow CPU access (needed to read vertices at runtime).
      lod_group: a LOD group name (LargeProp, SmallProp, HighDetail, ...).
Returns: {"path", "changed", "set": [...], "lods", "triangles", "nanite", "collision_prims"}.
Example: film-ue op assets.mesh path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair nanite=true collision=convex convex_hulls=8

ops.doc:
Move assets into a folder, keeping their names (references follow).

Re-import an asset from its source file (or from a new file), keeping its settings, with no dialog.

ops.summary: Delete assets safely: refused (code conflict, naming who) while another asset or the open level uses them,
ops.doc:
Delete assets safely: refused (code conflict, naming who) while another asset or the open level uses them,

Metadata tags on an asset (searchable by assets.find tags=...): set or remove key/values.

Converge a texture's settings: by role (base_color/emissive/translucency: sRGB colour; normal: TC_NORMALMAP

ops.name: assets.thumbnail
ops.summary: Pictures of an asset with no viewport: a temporary actor of it is placed away from the set, captured alone
ops.doc:
Pictures of an asset with no viewport: a temporary actor of it is placed away from the set, captured alone
(WP10's view.turntable with isolate), and removed. One view (a 3/4 shot) or several around it plus a sheet.
The open level's lights reach it only if it is placed among them (loc); `light` adds a temporary point light

Args: path: /Game/... StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh or Blueprint. out_dir: where the PNGs go on the box. views: how
      many. size_px: square size. elevation_deg/yaw_deg: the camera's angle above and around it. loc: where the
      temporary actor stands [x, y, z] cm (default far below the set). light: add a temporary key light.
Returns: {"path", "views": [{"yaw", "path"}], "sheet", "size_cm"}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op assets.thumbnail path=/Game/Props/SM_Chair out_dir=/tmp/thumbs/chair views=4

ops.doc:
A sequence's audio tracks and clips, with frames and seconds.

ops.summary: Import WAV files on the box as SoundWaves in `folder`, skipping any already there (idempotent).

Import WAV files on the box as SoundWaves in `folder`, skipping any already there (idempotent).

Import a timing document's voice lines and place each at its frame on one track: the voice, timed, in one call.

Args: sequence: LevelSequence path. timing: a timing document (filmtools.unreal.audio_timing:
{"kind": "timing", "fps", "lines": [{"id", "wav", "start_frame", ...}]}). folder: where the SoundWaves go.
track: the track's name. wav_root: a box directory the lines' relative `wav` paths are under. extend: lengthen

ops.summary: Put sounds on a named audio track of a sequence at their frames; re-running with the same clips changes nothing.

Put sounds on a named audio track of a sequence at their frames; re-running with the same clips changes nothing.

Args: sequence: LevelSequence path. clips: [{"sound": SoundWave path, "start_frame" (or "start_s"),
"end_frame" or "duration_s" (default: to the sound's end), "offset_s" (seconds into the sound, default 0),
"volume_db" (default 0), "fade_in_frames"/"fade_out_frames" (linear ramps from/to silence), "id"?}] or [sound, start_frame] pairs. track: the track's name ("VO", "Music", "SFX").
replace: the track holds exactly these clips (else they are added to it). extend: lengthen the playback range
to the last clip's end.
Returns: {"changed", "track", "clips": [{"sound", "start_frame", "end_frame", "row", "offset_s", "volume_db"}],
"end_frame"}.

ops.name: bridge.health

The bridge's state: engine, platform, project, uptime, protocol version, jobs, memory, idle cap, seconds

ops.name: cam.add
ops.summary: Make or converge a cine camera named `label`: place it, aim it, set its lens and focus.
ops.doc:
Make or converge a cine camera named `label`: place it, aim it, set its lens and focus.

Args: label: actor label. loc: [x, y, z] cm. rot_: {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} deg, or look_at: a point [x, y, z],
an actor label or "Label:Component:bone" (overrides rot_). focal_mm. aperture: f-stop. sensor_mm: [w, h] mm, or
filmback: a preset name ("16:9 Digital Film", the engine default; "16:9 DSLR" is full frame). lens_preset:
"50mm Prime f/1.8" etc. (sets the lens limits). focus_cm: manual focus distance; focus_on: a point/actor/bone
to focus on now (manual focus at its distance; for a moving subject key it with cam.move focus_on, or use
cam.focus mode=track).
A new camera gets the engine's default filmback and focal 35 mm unless given.

Numeric checks of a camera's frame on its subjects: QA's per-frame framing (headroom, cut-offs, feet, size, look

"hfov_deg"}}.

ops.summary: The coverage of a scene, all on one side of the line: for one subject a WS/MS/MCU/CU from 3/4 and a profile;
ops.doc:
The coverage of a scene, all on one side of the line: for one subject a WS/MS/MCU/CU from 3/4 and a profile;
for two or more a master, a two-shot, each one's MS/MCU/CU single and an over-the-shoulder. Makes a camera per

Args: side: left|right of the line from the first subject to the second, seen from above.
Returns: {"line", "side", "shots": [{"name", "camera", "kind", "size", "focal", "distance", "loc", "rot",

ops.name: cam.focus
ops.summary: Set a camera's focus: mode "manual" (distance_cm, or the distance to `target` now), "track" (follow an actor,
ops.doc:
Set a camera's focus: mode "manual" (distance_cm, or the distance to `target` now), "track" (follow an actor,
the engine's tracking focus: `target` an actor label, or "eyes:Label" for its eyes at the current pose, or
"Label:Component:bone"), or "off" (no depth of field).

Args: offset: cm in the tracked actor's own frame, added to the target. smooth_speed: >0 smooths focus changes.
Example: film-ue op cam.focus label=CAM_A mode=track target=eyes:Presenter

ops.name: cam.frame
ops.summary: Frame subjects with a camera by shot grammar: "MCU of Presenter from 3/4 left, eye level, 50 mm".
ops.doc:
Frame subjects with a camera by shot grammar: "MCU of Presenter from 3/4 left, eye level, 50 mm".

Args: camera: label (made if missing). subjects: an actor label or a list (a two-shot, a group).
size: ECU CU MCU MS COWBOY MWS WS EWS (aliases: close-up, medium, wide, full...). angle: degrees or front, 3/4,
profile, 3/4 back, back: around from the first subject's facing toward its own `side` (left|right).
height: eye, high, low, slight high, slight low, overhead, worm, degrees, shoulder/chest/hip/knee/ground, or
{"z": cm}. focal_mm (distance solved) or distance_cm with focal_mm=None (focal solved; snap_focal rounds to a
prime). place: auto (thirds with lead room off-axis, centre when frontal), center, left third, right third, or
u 0..1. headroom: v of the head's top (default per size). dutch_deg: roll. focus: focus on the first subject's
eyes. apply: False only plans (nothing changes).
Returns: {"camera": cam.describe dict, "solve": {distance, focal, error, predicted u/v of every landmark,
dof, warnings}, "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op cam.frame camera=CAM_A subjects=Presenter size=MCU angle=3/4 side=left focal_mm=50

ops.name: cam.move
ops.summary: Key camera moves into a sequence: dolly, push_in, pull_out, truck, pedestal, crane, orbit/arc, pan, tilt,
ops.doc:
Key camera moves into a sequence: dolly, push_in, pull_out, truck, pedestal, crane, orbit/arc, pan, tilt,
roll, zoom, dolly_zoom, whip, rack, follow, hold; eased, one after another from the camera's current pose, with
optional handheld noise. Replaces the camera's transform (and focal/focus) tracks in that sequence.

Args: moves_: [{"move": kind, "frames": n | "from"/"to", "ease": in_out|in|out|linear|sine|smooth|expo, ...}]
(cam.presets lists kinds; docs/unreal/camera.md their arguments). aim: what the camera keeps framed (a point, an
actor label, "Label:Component:bone", "eyes:Label"). focus_on: the same, baked as a follow-focus. noise: "subtle"
| "handheld" | "documentary" | "breathing" | "shake" or {"preset", "seed", "scale", "pos", "rot", "hz"}.
step: frames between baked keys. end_frame: hold the last pose to there.
A multi-tick job (the keys go in one batched seq.apply when WP8's core is there).
Returns: {"keys": {"transform", "focal", "focus"}, "segments", "first", "last", "write", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op cam.move camera=CAM_A sequence=/Game/Seq/S1 'moves_=[{"move":"push_in","fraction":0.2,"frames":72}]' aim=eyes:Presenter

ops.name: cam.point
ops.summary: Where a target is now, in world cm: a point, an actor label (its location; with `offset` in its own frame),
ops.doc:
Where a target is now, in world cm: a point, an actor label (its location; with `offset` in its own frame),
"Label:Component:bone", "eyes:Label" (between its eyes), or a camera's label (its lens).

Example: film-ue op cam.point target=eyes:Presenter

ops.name: cam.presets
ops.summary: The filmback and lens presets (the engine's own, from BaseEngine.ini) and the shot sizes, angles and heights
ops.doc:
The filmback and lens presets (the engine's own, from BaseEngine.ini) and the shot sizes, angles and heights
the framing solver knows.

Returns: {"filmbacks": {name: [w_mm, h_mm]}, "lenses": {name: {...}}, "default_filmback", "sizes": {key: desc},
"angles", "heights", "moves", "noise"}.
Example: film-ue op cam.presets

ops.name: cam.project
ops.summary: Where things land in a camera's frame: u, v (0..1 from the top left; outside = out of frame) and depth (cm),
ops.doc:
Where things land in a camera's frame: u, v (0..1 from the top left; outside = out of frame) and depth (cm),
for named points ({"name": [x, y, z] | label | "Label:Component:bone"}) and every landmark of `subjects`.

Example: film-ue op cam.project camera=CAM_A subjects=Presenter

ops.name: cam.remove
ops.summary: Delete cine cameras (and rigs) by label or by label prefix; missing ones are skipped.
ops.doc:
Delete cine cameras (and rigs) by label or by label prefix; missing ones are skipped.

Example: film-ue op cam.remove prefix=CAM_

ops.name: cam.rig
ops.summary: A camera rail or crane (the engine's CameraRig_Rail / CameraRig_Crane), with `camera` mounted on it.
ops.doc:
A camera rail or crane (the engine's CameraRig_Rail / CameraRig_Crane), with `camera` mounted on it.

rail: `points` [[x, y, z], ...] world cm along the track (2+); `position` 0..1 along it; lock_orientation turns
the camera with the rail. crane: at `loc`, turned `yaw_deg`, arm `arm_cm` long, raised `pitch_deg`. Drive either
over time with cam.rig_move.
Example: film-ue op cam.rig label=Rail_A kind=rail 'points=[[300,-200,150],[300,200,150]]' camera=CAM_A

ops.name: cam.rig_move
ops.summary: Animate a rig in a sequence: a rail's position along it (0..1), a crane's pitch, yaw and arm.
ops.doc:
Animate a rig in a sequence: a rail's position along it (0..1), a crane's pitch, yaw and arm.

Args: keys: [[frame, {"position": 0..1} | {"pitch_deg", "yaw_deg", "arm_cm"}], ...] (auto-eased).
Example: film-ue op cam.rig_move rig_label=Rail_A sequence=/Game/Seq/S1 'keys=[[0,{"position":0}],[96,{"position":1}]]'

ops.name: cam.set
ops.summary: Change an existing camera's lens: focal length (or the horizontal field of view it gives), aperture,
ops.doc:
Change an existing camera's lens: focal length (or the horizontal field of view it gives), aperture,
filmback, lens limits, near clip plane.

Example: film-ue op cam.set label=CAM_A focal_mm=85 aperture=1.8

ops.name: cam.shoot
ops.summary: Frame a camera from a sentence of shot grammar: "medium close-up of Host from 30 deg left at eye level, 50mm",
ops.doc:
Frame a camera from a sentence of shot grammar: "medium close-up of Host from 30 deg left at eye level, 50mm",
"two-shot of Host and Guest, low angle, 35mm", "CU of Guest from 3/4 right, 2 m away" (the focal length solved).
The subjects are the level's actor labels found in the text. Words it does not understand are returned in
`unparsed` (nothing is guessed); the vocabulary is in docs/unreal/camera.md.

Returns: cam.frame's result plus {"parsed": the arguments it read, "words": the camera described back}.
Example: film-ue op cam.shoot camera=CAM_A text='MCU of Host from 3/4 left, eye level, 50mm'

ops.name: cam.still
ops.summary: A still through a camera with the operator's guides drawn on it: thirds, action/title safe, centre, and each
ops.doc:
A still through a camera with the operator's guides drawn on it: thirds, action/title safe, centre, and each
subject's landmarks where the lens math puts them (green crosses), so a mismatch between solver and render shows.
A multi-tick job. Keep it small (960x540): the overlay is drawn in pure Python.

Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "raw": the still without guides}.
Example: film-ue op cam.still camera=CAM_A out=/tmp/cam_a.png subjects=Presenter

ops.name: cam.subject
ops.summary: What the framing solver sees of an actor: its landmarks (head_top, eyes, nose, mouth, chin, neck, shoulders,
ops.doc:
What the framing solver sees of an actor: its landmarks (head_top, eyes, nose, mouth, chin, neck, shoulders,
chest, waist, hips, knees, ankles, feet) in world cm, its facing and height, and whether they came from its
skeleton or its bounds.

Args: target: actor label. mode: auto (bones, else bounds) | bones | bounds. facing: [x, y, z] override.
top_z: the crown's height when hair or a hat makes it higher than the default (eyes + 11.5 cm).
Example: film-ue op cam.subject target=Presenter

ops.name: editor.console
ops.summary: Run one console command in the editor (stat, r.*, Fab.Login, ...). It cannot report the command's own output:
ops.doc:
Run one console command in the editor (stat, r.*, Fab.Login, ...). It cannot report the command's own output:
read the log (film-ue log) or a cvar after it. Never run Fab.Logout or Fab.SetEnvironment: both delete the
saved Epic sign-in.

Args: command: the command line as typed in the console.
Returns: {"command", "ran": true}.
Example: film-ue op editor.console 'command=stat unit'

ops.name: editor.cvar
ops.summary: Read a console variable, or set it (through the console, as typed there) and read it back.
ops.doc:
Read a console variable, or set it (through the console, as typed there) and read it back.

Args: name: e.g. "r.RayTracing". value: the new value (number, bool or string); omit to only read.
Returns: {"name", "value": the value now (string), "before", "changed": bool}.
Example: film-ue op editor.cvar name=t.MaxFPS value=30

ops.name: editor.describe
ops.summary: What the editor is and how it is doing: engine, platform, RHI, project, open level, unsaved packages, idle cap,
ops.doc:
What the editor is and how it is doing: engine, platform, RHI, project, open level, unsaved packages, idle cap,
shader workers, memory, bridge jobs.

Returns: {"engine", "platform", "python", "rhi", "project", "level", "dirty": {"maps", "content"},
"idle_fps", "max_fps", "shader_workers", "rss_mb", "jobs": {"queued", "running"}, "uptime_s"}.
Example: film-ue op editor.describe

ops.name: editor.doctor
ops.summary: Check that this editor can do the work: engine 5.8, Python 3.11, a real GPU RHI (not -nullrhi), the plugins
ops.doc:
Check that this editor can do the work: engine 5.8, Python 3.11, a real GPU RHI (not -nullrhi), the plugins
the ops need, every op module imported, free disk, the Epic sign-in (Linux), the render/MetaHuman/data layer
APIs reachable from Python, and the hair sky-lighting trap. Read-only.

Returns: {"pass": no fail-severity issue, "issues": [{"code", "severity", "message", "fix"}], "metrics":
{"engine", "python", "platform", "rhi", "offscreen", "free_gb", "plugins_missing", "ops", "broken"}}.
Example: film-ue doctor   (or: film-ue op editor.doctor)

ops.name: editor.gc
ops.summary: Collect garbage (frees unreferenced objects after big imports or level changes) and report memory.
ops.doc:
Collect garbage (frees unreferenced objects after big imports or level changes) and report memory.

Returns: {"rss_mb_before", "rss_mb_after"} (Linux; None elsewhere).
Example: film-ue op editor.gc

ops.name: editor.idle
ops.summary: Cap an offscreen editor between jobs so it does not hold the GPU at full load: the frame rate (t.MaxFPS) and
ops.doc:
Cap an offscreen editor between jobs so it does not hold the GPU at full load: the frame rate (t.MaxFPS) and
whether the level viewport redraws every frame. Movie Render Queue lifts the cap while it renders (render.mrq).

Args: fps: the cap (0 = none). realtime: the level viewport in realtime.
Returns: {"fps", "realtime", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op editor.idle fps=10

ops.name: editor.wait_compile
ops.summary: Wait until the editor has no shader compiling (no ShaderCompileWorker for `settle_s` seconds), ticking all the
ops.doc:
Wait until the editor has no shader compiling (no ShaderCompileWorker for `settle_s` seconds), ticking all the
while, then (finish) let the engine finish any asset compilation left. The first open of a project on a new box
compiles for many minutes: run this before stills or renders.

Args: timeout_s: give up after this long (an error with code "timeout"). settle_s: how long the workers must
stay at zero. finish: then call the engine's finish-all-compilation (blocks briefly).
Returns: {"waited_s", "workers_max", "finished": bool}. Multi-tick (reports progress).
Example: film-ue op editor.wait_compile timeout_s=3600

ops.name: fab.add
ops.summary: Add a Fab asset to the project from its signed download URL (what the Fab page hands the plugin's
ops.doc:
Add a Fab asset to the project from its signed download URL (what the Fab page hands the plugin's
AddToProject; tools/filmtools/unreal/fab_shim.py gets it for a listing without a window): download (no auth:
the URL is signed), unzip into the plugin's cache, import as fab.import does. With the FabScript project plugin
installed (unreal/plugins/FabScript) and metadata given, Epic's own AddToProject runs instead, for every format
(including unreal-engine packs).

Multi-tick: downloads in the background and yields until done.
Args: url: the signed download URL. metadata: {"AssetId", "AssetName", "AssetType" (gltf|fbx|unreal-engine|...),
      "ListingType", "AssetNamespace", "DistributionPointBaseUrls", "IsQuixel"} as the page gives it.
      dest: content folder. replace: import again over an earlier import.
Returns: fab.import's result plus {"download": file on the box, "route": "python"|"native"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.add url=<signed url> 'metadata={"AssetId": "abc", "AssetName": "Rock", "IsQuixel": true}'

ops.name: fab.import
ops.summary: Import a Fab or Megascans download that is on the box (a zip, or a folder): Fab-plugin format (one .gltf +
ops.doc:
Import a Fab or Megascans download that is on the box (a zip, or a folder): Fab-plugin format (one .gltf +
.json) the way the plugin does it (Interchange with InterchangeMegascansPipeline, per type: 3D Nanite, plants,
surfaces, decals), any other glTF/FBX/OBJ/USD with the generic importer, loose textures as a PBR material.

Args: path: zip or folder on the box (e.g. /tmp/FabLibrary/<AssetId>/x.zip). dest: content folder (default
      /Game/Fab/Megascans/<Type>/<Name>_<id>/<Tier> like the plugin, or /Game/Fab/<Name>). kind: force the
      Megascans type (3D, Plants, Surfaces, Decals, Imperfections). replace: re-import over what is there (else
      an imported asset is kept: changed false).
Returns: {"format", "dest", "imported": [paths], "material": path|None, "changed", "meta"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.import path=/data/fab/rock_4k.zip

ops.name: fab.library
ops.summary: The signed-in account's Fab library (what it owns), from the endpoint the plugin's My Folder uses
ops.doc:
The signed-in account's Fab library (what it owns), from the endpoint the plugin's My Folder uses
(GET <fab>/e/accounts/<account>/ue/library, FabMyFolderIntegration.cpp): title, asset id, listing type, the
page url, and a thumbnail url.

Args: query: keep items whose title/description contain these words. limit: at most this many. account_id: the
      Epic account (default: from the token).
Returns: {"items": [{"title", "asset_id", "asset_namespace", "listing_type", "url", "image", "source"}],
         "count", "next_cursor"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.library query=chair

ops.name: fab.login
ops.summary: Sign Fab in: by default with the saved sign-in (opening a Fab tab is what makes the plugin try it, and then
ops.doc:
Sign Fab in: by default with the saved sign-in (opening a Fab tab is what makes the plugin try it, and then
the editor's -AUTH_TYPE=exchangecode -AUTH_PASSWORD=<code> if that fails); with portal, start the device-code
sign-in (Fab.Login): its code and URL are in the editor log for a person to approve once.

Multi-tick: waits up to timeout_s for the sign-in. Already signed in: changes nothing.
Args: portal: device-code sign-in instead of the saved one. timeout_s: how long to wait.
Returns: {"signed_in", "changed", "method", "waited_s", "hint"}.
Example: film-ue op fab.login

ops.name: fab.status
ops.summary: Is Fab usable from code here: plugin loaded, signed in, a saved sign-in on disk, the pack installer library
ops.doc:
Is Fab usable from code here: plugin loaded, signed in, a saved sign-in on disk, the pack installer library
(Linux needs ThirdParty/libBuildPatchInstallerLib.so for unreal-engine-format packs), the download cache.

Returns: {"plugin", "signed_in", "saved_sign_ins": int, "pack_installer": bool, "cache_dir", "platform",
         "next": what to do}. No token is returned.
Example: film-ue op fab.status

ops.name: jobs.cancel
ops.summary: Cancel a queued job, or a running multi-tick one (it stops at its next step and runs its clean-up).
ops.doc:
Cancel a queued job, or a running multi-tick one (it stops at its next step and runs its clean-up).

Args: id: the job id.
Returns: {"ok", "state", "changed"}.
Example: film-ue op jobs.cancel id=3f2a9c1b0d4e

ops.name: jobs.get
ops.summary: One job: its state and progress, and when finished its result or error.
ops.doc:
One job: its state and progress, and when finished its result or error.

Args: id: the job id (from an async call or jobs.list).
Returns: the job: {"id", "state", "done", "ok", "result", "error", "progress", "message", ...}.
Example: film-ue op jobs.get id=3f2a9c1b0d4e

ops.name: jobs.list
ops.summary: Recent jobs, newest first, without their results.
ops.doc:
Recent jobs, newest first, without their results.

Args: state: queued|running|done|failed|cancelled|lost ("" = all). name: an op-name prefix ("render."). limit.
Returns: [{"id", "name", "state", "progress", "message", "created", "started", "finished", "ms"}].
Example: film-ue op jobs.list state=running

ops.name: layout.align
ops.summary: Line actors up along one axis by their bounds: their min edges, max edges or centres on a common value
ops.doc:
Line actors up along one axis by their bounds: their min edges, max edges or centres on a common value
(`ref_cm`, the same edge of `ref_label`, or the group's extreme / mean).

Example: film-ue op layout.align 'labels=["Book_00","Book_01","Book_02"]' axis=y to=max

ops.name: layout.array
ops.summary: Lay out `count` copies of an asset (or a basic shape) as a row, a grid or a circle, labelled
ops.doc:
Lay out `count` copies of an asset (or a basic shape) as a row, a grid or a circle, labelled
`<prefix>_00`, `<prefix>_01`, ...; re-running moves the same actors, and a smaller count removes the extras.

Args: pattern: row (start + k * step_cm), grid (rows of `cols`, X by step_cm[0], Y by step_cm[1]) or circle
(around `center`, radius_cm, from start_deg over arc_deg, counter-clockwise from above). face: none (yaw_deg),
center (circle: each faces the centre), out (faces away). drop: rest each on what is under it.
Returns: {"changed", "labels", "made", "moved", "removed"}.
Example: film-ue op layout.array prefix=Chair asset=/Game/Props/SM_Chair pattern=circle count=6 \
         'center=[0,0,0]' radius_cm=120 face=center

ops.name: layout.distribute
ops.summary: Space actors evenly along an axis, in the order given: centres from start_cm to end_cm (default: the first
ops.doc:
Space actors evenly along an axis, in the order given: centres from start_cm to end_cm (default: the first
and last actors' current centres), or edge to edge `gap_cm` apart starting at the first one.

Example: film-ue op layout.distribute 'labels=["A","B","C","D"]' axis=x gap_cm=20

ops.name: layout.drop
ops.summary: Rest each actor on whatever is under it: its bounds' bottom on the highest support below its centre whose
ops.doc:
Rest each actor on whatever is under it: its bounds' bottom on the highest support below its centre whose
footprint overlaps (a table top, a rug, a riser), else on `floor_z`. Actors are dropped in the order given, so
list a table before the cup that sits on it.

Args: labels: actors to drop. floor_z: the floor height in cm (None for no floor: an actor over nothing stays
put). gap_cm: lift above the support. mode: bounds (boxes, deterministic) or trace (a line trace down; needs
collision).
Returns: {"changed": bool, "moved": {label: dz_cm}, "unsupported": [labels with nothing under them]}.
Example: film-ue op layout.drop 'labels=["Desk","Lamp","Mug"]'

ops.name: layout.relative
ops.summary: Put `label` at an offset in another actor's frame: [forward, right, up] cm from `of` along its own yaw (a
ops.doc:
Put `label` at an offset in another actor's frame: [forward, right, up] cm from `of` along its own yaw (a
chair 80 cm in front of a desk: offset_cm=[80, 0, 0]), then turn it and rest it on what is under it.

Args: face: toward (look at `of`), away, same (copy its yaw), none (keep), or fixed (use yaw_deg).
Returns: {"changed", "loc", "rot"}.
Example: film-ue op layout.relative label=Chair of=Desk 'offset_cm=[80,0,0]' face=toward

ops.name: layout.remove
ops.summary: Remove every actor a layout.array / layout.scatter with this prefix made (by its tag, not by name).
ops.doc:
Remove every actor a layout.array / layout.scatter with this prefix made (by its tag, not by name).

Example: film-ue op layout.remove prefix=Rock

ops.name: layout.scatter
ops.summary: Scatter up to `count` copies of an asset over a rectangle, no two closer than min_dist_cm, deterministic for
ops.doc:
Scatter up to `count` copies of an asset over a rectangle, no two closer than min_dist_cm, deterministic for
a seed (Poisson disk), with random yaw and uniform scale in ranges; labelled `<prefix>_00`...; re-running with
the same seed gives the same layout, a new seed a new one.

Args: region: [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] cm. exclude: rectangles to keep clear ([[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] each). avoid:
actor labels whose footprints (plus min_dist_cm / 2) are kept clear. z: height before dropping. drop: rest each
on what is under it.
Returns: {"changed", "labels", "made", "moved", "removed", "placed": n} (n < count when the region is full).
Example: film-ue op layout.scatter prefix=Rock asset=/Game/Env/SM_Rock count=30 \
         'region=[[-1000,-1000],[1000,1000]]' min_dist_cm=150 seed=7 'avoid=["Path"]'

ops.name: layout.settle
ops.summary: Let props fall and come to rest under physics, then keep where they landed (a pile of books, a dropped
ops.doc:
Let props fall and come to rest under physics, then keep where they landed (a pile of books, a dropped
cushion, a chair knocked over): runs Simulate in Editor for `seconds`, reads each actor's resting transform from
the simulated world and writes it back onto the editor actor. Multi-tick. The actors' meshes need collision, and
so does what they land on.

Args: labels: actors to simulate (made Movable, physics on for the run; restored after unless keep_physics).
seconds: simulated time to let them settle. start_timeout_s: how long to wait for Simulate to start.
Returns: {"changed", "moved": {label: {"loc", "rot", "dist_cm"}}, "still": [labels that did not move > 0.5 cm]}.
Example: film-ue op layout.settle 'labels=["Book_00","Book_01","Cushion"]' seconds=3

ops.name: layout.snap
ops.summary: Snap actor locations to a grid (X and Y; Z untouched) and, with yaw_step_deg, their yaw to multiples of it.
ops.doc:
Snap actor locations to a grid (X and Y; Z untouched) and, with yaw_step_deg, their yaw to multiples of it.

Example: film-ue op layout.snap 'labels=["Desk","Chair"]' grid_cm=5 yaw_step_deg=15

ops.name: level.actors
ops.summary: The open level's actors: [label, class, location].
ops.doc: The open level's actors: [label, class, location].

ops.name: level.bone
ops.summary: World locations of bones/sockets on an actor's skeletal mesh component.
ops.doc: World locations of bones/sockets on an actor's skeletal mesh component.

ops.summary: Delete actors by label (missing ones are skipped).
ops.doc: Delete actors by label (missing ones are skipped).

ops.name: level.describe
ops.summary: The open level at a glance: its path, actor count by class, lights, cameras, the overall bounds of visible
ops.doc:
The open level at a glance: its path, actor count by class, lights, cameras, the overall bounds of visible
geometry, and every actor (as level.find) with `actors`.

Example: film-ue op level.describe

ops.name: level.find
ops.summary: Actors matching every filter given, as JSON (label, class, loc, rot, scale, bounds, tags, folder, mesh).

Actors matching every filter given, as JSON (label, class, loc, rot, scale, bounds, tags, folder, mesh).

ops.name: level.folder
ops.summary: Put actors in an outliner folder (`Set/Props`; '' for none): grouping that scene.describe and level.find
ops.doc:
Put actors in an outliner folder (`Set/Props`; '' for none): grouping that scene.describe and level.find
can filter on.

Example: film-ue op level.folder 'labels=["Desk","Chair"]' path=Office/Furniture

ops.name: level.get
ops.summary: One actor in detail: what level.find gives plus its components (name, class, and for meshes their mesh and
ops.doc:
One actor in detail: what level.find gives plus its components (name, class, and for meshes their mesh and
materials).

ops.name: level.layer_add
ops.summary: Put actors in a data layer, making the layer (its DataLayerAsset under asset_dir and its instance in this
ops.doc:
Put actors in a data layer, making the layer (its DataLayerAsset under asset_dir and its instance in this
level) when it does not exist yet. Re-running changes nothing.

Returns: {"changed", "created": bool, "added": [labels newly in it]}.
Example: film-ue op level.layer_add name=Props_Night 'labels=["Lamp","Candle"]'

ops.name: level.layer_remove
ops.summary: Take actors out of a data layer (actors not in it are skipped).
ops.doc:
Take actors out of a data layer (actors not in it are skipped).

Example: film-ue op level.layer_remove name=Props_Night 'labels=["Lamp"]'

ops.name: level.layer_set

subsurface_profile|two_sided_foliage|cloth|clear_coat|thin_translucent|hair|eye, "two_sided": bool,
"domain": surface|deferred_decal|post_process|light_function|ui, "translucency_lighting": surface_per_pixel|...,
"usage": [skeletal_mesh, instanced, nanite, groom, morph_targets, ...], "opacity_mask_clip": 0.333,
"nodes": {id: {"type": Scalar|Vector|Texture|Switch|Const|Multiply|Add|Lerp|OneMinus|Power|TexCoord|Fresnel|
VertexColor|Function|... or any MaterialExpression class, "in": {pin: "node" | "node.R" | number | [r,g,b]},
other keys: editor properties (name, default, texture, sampler: color|normal|masks|linear_color|grayscale)}},

ops.name: mh.cloth_inflate
ops.summary: Push a garment out along its normals by `cm`, so skin under tight cloth stops poking through. A multi-tick job.
ops.doc:
Push a garment out along its normals by `cm`, so skin under tight cloth stops poking through. A multi-tick job.

Nothing the renderer is drawing is ever edited: a material in use that is reparented or recompiled while frames
render trips `UniformExpressionCache... == Material.GetRenderingThreadShaderMap()` and takes the editor down (it
did, right after a MetaHuman rebuild had made fresh garment instances). So the worn instance is copied to
`{folder}/{label}_<name>_Inflate`, the copy is parented on project copies of its plugin chain whose master gains a
World Position Offset (normal x FM_Inflate), every shader finishes compiling, the editor ticks a few frames, and
only then does the component swap to the copy. A master already in use is never recompiled (a new one is made);
re-running on an inflated garment only changes the amount, a plain parameter change that is safe. `which` limits it
to the garments whose material name contains it (e.g. "Shirt": a top pushed out over shorts that stay put, else
both move together and the shorts' waistband still shows through the tee); others already inflated go back to 0.

Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"exposure", "histogram" (32 bins of luma), "regions"}}.
Example: film-ue op qa.exposure image=/tmp/qa/a.png 'target_stops=[-2,-0.5]'

(an object over a floor without collision reads as unsupported).

ops.name: qa.framing

ops.doc:
How subjects sit in a camera's frame, measured from their bones (characters) or bounds (anything else).

Args: subjects: actor labels. camera: a camera label; "" with sequence+frame: the cut's camera at that frame
(the sequence is scrubbed there first so animated cameras and bodies are where the shot has them).
expect: intent per subject or for all: {"size": "MCU"|["MS","MCU"], "headroom": [lo, hi], "side":
"left"|"right"|"center", "in_frame": 1.0}, or {"Ada": {...}, "Ben": {...}}. width_px/height_px: the output

Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"camera", "subjects": {label: {size, box, headroom, eyes, looks,
look_room}}}, "still"?}. Multi-tick when sequence or still_out is given.
Example: film-ue op qa.framing 'subjects=["Ada"]' camera=CamA 'expect={"size":"MCU"}'

ops.name: qa.image
ops.summary: Exposure, clipping, colour and focus of a PNG on the box, as numbers and issues.
ops.doc:
Exposure, clipping, colour and focus of a PNG on the box, as numbers and issues.

ops.summary: Actors whose bounds interpenetrate (a chair sunk into a table, two props in one place).
ops.doc:
Actors whose bounds interpenetrate (a chair sunk into a table, two props in one place).

Args: labels: the actors (default every visible mesh actor). ignore: labels to skip (the floor, walls, the
set's shell). ignore_pairs: [[a, b]] that may overlap (a book on a shelf). min_fraction: the share of the
smaller box that counts. touching_cm: resting contact allowed.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"pairs": [[a, b, fraction, depth_cm]]}}. Axis-aligned bounds: confirm a hit

ops.name: qa.parts

ops.doc:

ops.name: qa.penetration
ops.summary: Body showing through clothes, measured as the viewer would see it: two depth captures from each view (the
ops.doc:
Body showing through clothes, measured as the viewer would see it: two depth captures from each view (the
body parts alone, the garments alone); where a garment covers a pixel and the body is nearer by more than

Args: label: the character. body/garments: component names (default a MetaHuman's Body+Face / Torso+Legs+Feet;
qa.parts lists them), or labels of other actors whose meshes form that layer. camera: look from this camera (with sequence+frame: the shot's camera and pose); views: N
views around the character instead (or as well), at elevation_deg. size_px: capture size (square for views;
the camera's aspect otherwise). out_dir: write a still per view with the penetrating pixels painted magenta.
Returns: {"pass", "issues", "metrics": {"views": {name: {fraction, pixels, worst_cm, box}}, "worst_fraction"}}.
Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op qa.penetration label=Ada views=6 out_dir=/tmp/qa/pen

ops.name: qa.review
ops.summary: Everything wrong with a shot, a sequence or a set, in one JSON and one picture.
ops.doc:
Everything wrong with a shot, a sequence or a set, in one JSON and one picture.

For each frame (sequence: `frames`, or `per_shot` per camera cut; no sequence: one still through `camera`) it
takes a still, measures exposure and colour, frames every subject (headroom, cuts, size), compares with
`reference_dir`/{frame:05d}.png when given, and (with "penetration") checks garments from the shot's camera;
once for the scene it checks floating and overlapping props; across cuts it checks exposure/colour continuity.

Args: out_dir: where frames, review.json and review.png go. sequence/frames/per_shot/camera: what to look at.
subjects: characters/props to frame (default every visible character). expect: per-subject or global intent
for qa.framing, plus {"image": {...}} for qa.image (e.g. {"image": {"stops": [-3,-1]}}). checks: a subset of
image, framing, penetration, floating, overlaps, continuity, reference (default all but penetration).
ignore: labels skipped by floating/overlaps (floor, walls). mode: still mode (view.still). baseline: a baseline
suite: each frame's still is checked against <suite>/<frame> (qa.baseline_check, `baseline_mode` auto: the first
run makes the baselines, later runs regress against them).
Returns: {"pass", "verdict", "counts", "summary": [lines, worst first], "issues", "metrics": {"frames"},
"report": review.json path, "image": review.png path}. Multi-tick; ~1 s a frame with mode=capture.
Example: film-ue op qa.review sequence=/Game/Seq/S010 out_dir=/tmp/qa/s010 per_shot=2

ops.name: qa.snapshot

ops.doc:
The level's state as JSON for later diffs: every actor's class, transform, bounds, visibility, materials,

Args: out: also write it to this file. labels: only these actors.
Returns: {"actors": {label: {class, loc, rot, scale, bounds, hidden, mesh, materials, props}}, "meta"}.

ops.name: render.encode
ops.summary: Encode a render's frames into video with ffmpeg on the box: H.264 (yuv420p, CRF), H.265 or ProRes (prores_ks,
ops.doc:
Encode a render's frames into video with ffmpeg on the box: H.264 (yuv420p, CRF), H.265 or ProRes (prores_ks,
10-bit), with the render's WAV chunks laid on the timeline (or an audio file of yours). Frames must be complete

Args: spec: the RENDER SPEC that rendered them. start/end: frames, end exclusive (default the spec's range).
outputs: video outputs (default the spec's h264/h265/prores outputs, else one h264).
Returns: {"videos": [{"kind", "path", "frames", "start", "end", "audio", "bytes"}], "changed", "fps"}.
Example: film-ue op render.encode 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel", "out_dir": "/srv/r/reel"}' 'outputs=[{"kind": "prores", "profile": 3}]'

ops.name: render.frames
ops.summary: Render a few frames of a sequence through its camera cuts with MRQ, viewport-free (works offscreen on Linux):
ops.doc:
Render a few frames of a sequence through its camera cuts with MRQ, viewport-free (works offscreen on Linux):
for stills, contact sheets and checks (WP10's qa.still mode=mrq builds on it). Consecutive frames in one cut are
one MRQ job, pre-rolled from the cut start. Frames already on disk are reused.

Args: sequence: /Game/... level sequence. frames: sequence frame numbers. out_dir: directory on the box.
level: map (default the open one). preset: preview|draft|final|... width/height: pixels (default the preset's).
cvars: extra console variables. overwrite: render again even when the frame is on disk (out_dir shared with
other stills, or the scene changed since).
Returns: {"frames": {frame: png/jpg path}, "cameras": {frame: camera label}, "width", "height", "seconds",
"changed", "report"}.
Example: film-ue op render.frames sequence=/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel 'frames=[1200,1260]' out_dir=/srv/r/stills

ops.name: render.gpu
ops.summary: The render box's GPU and memory now: name, VRAM total/used/free in GB, utilisation, and the editor's RSS.
ops.doc:
The render box's GPU and memory now: name, VRAM total/used/free in GB, utilisation, and the editor's RSS.

Returns: {"gpu": {"name", "total_gb", "used_gb", "free_gb", "util_pct"} | None, "rss_gb", "rendering": bool}.
Example: film-ue op render.gpu

ops.name: render.job
ops.summary: Render a RENDER SPEC to the end (multi-tick: the bridge returns a job id at once with wait=false; follow it,
ops.doc:
Render a RENDER SPEC to the end (multi-tick: the bridge returns a job id at once with wait=false; follow it,
or render.status): plan the chunks, check the level and the GPU, render each chunk with MRQ (pre-rolled from its
shot start), watch frames, VRAM and stalls, then write <out_dir>/_render/<name>.report.json. Re-running resumes:
frames on disk (and complete) are skipped, so a finished job re-runs as a no-op.

Args: spec: the RENDER SPEC. stall_s: cancel a chunk after this many seconds with no new frame.
Returns: the report: {"status": ok|incomplete|failed|stalled|vram_abort|cancelled, "changed", "frames",
"seconds", "chunks": [{"id", "status", "frames", "missing", "median_s", "vram_peak_gb", "errors", ...}],
"measured": {"s_per_frame", "sample_s_1080p"}, "report": path, "errors"}.
Example: film-ue op render.job --no-wait 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel", "out_dir": "/srv/r/reel", "preset": "final", "shots": ["Reel_S16"]}'

ops.name: render.manifest
ops.summary: Write, per chunk of a spec, an MRQ queue manifest and the command line that renders it in a process with no
ops.doc:
Write, per chunk of a spec, an MRQ queue manifest and the command line that renders it in a process with no
editor (one process per job: survives editor restarts; run it on this box or another with the same project).

Returns: {"changed": True, "chunks": [{"id", "start", "end", "manifest", "argv"}], "exit_codes"}.
Example: film-ue op render.manifest 'spec={"sequence": "/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel", "out_dir": "/srv/r/reel", "executor": "cmdline"}'

ops.name: render.mrq
ops.summary: Start one Movie Render Queue job and return at once (poll render.progress); render.job does a whole spec.
ops.doc:
Start one Movie Render Queue job and return at once (poll render.progress); render.job does a whole spec.
Frames go to `out_dir` as {frame}.png|exr|jpg, the audio as a wav; `start`/`end` (end exclusive) render part of
the sequence. `preroll_from`: the shot's first frame when `start` is mid-shot: the frames between are evaluated
without rendering so cloth arrives as in a full-shot render (needs the camera cut to begin there). `executor`:
"pie" (in this editor) or "process" (a separate -game process; offscreen where the editor has no desktop). The
process loads the level from disk, and with unsaved changes the executor asks to save first: unattended, that
question goes unanswered and the job never starts, so unsaved packages are an error unless `save_dirty`.

Example: film-ue op render.mrq sequence=/Game/Reel/SEQ_Reel level=/Game/Studio/Studio out_dir=/srv/r/s16 start=1196 end=1220

ops.name: render.plan
ops.summary: What a render spec would do, without rendering: the resolved settings, one chunk per camera cut (or per
ops.doc:

Args: spec: a RENDER SPEC (docs/unreal/render.md; schema tools/filmtools/unreal/schemas/render.schema.json).
Returns: {"name", "spec", "range", "chunks": [{"id", "camera", "start", "end", "frames", "preroll", "seconds"}],

ops.name: seq.anim
ops.summary: Animation sections on an actor's skeletal mesh component (a MetaHuman's "Body" or "Face"), each
ops.doc:
Animation sections on an actor's skeletal mesh component (a MetaHuman's "Body" or "Face"), each
{"anim", "start", "end", "offset", "blend_in", "blend_out", "rate", "weight", "loop", "row"}: `start`/`end`

Sounds in a sequence on a named audio track ("VO", "Score", "SFX"): clips [{"sound", "start", "end", "offset",

ops.name: seq.key_collection
ops.summary: Key a scalar parameter of a material parameter collection (look.collection) on the sequence's track for that
ops.doc:
Key a scalar parameter of a material parameter collection (look.collection) on the sequence's track for that
collection: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...]. Sequencer writes the world's instance of the collection, so the
value reaches every material reading it with no mesh binding and no MID in between. Replaces only that
parameter's keys.

ops.name: seq.key_color
ops.summary: Key a colour property: keys [[frame, [r, g, b(, a)](, interp)], ...]. An FColor property (a light's
ops.doc:
Key a colour property: keys [[frame, [r, g, b(, a)](, interp)], ...]. An FColor property (a light's
"LightColor") takes sRGB 0-1, as look.light does; an FLinearColor one (fog "FogInscatteringLuminance", a post
"Settings.ColorGain") takes linear values. `srgb` overrides that guess. Component and replacement as key_float.

ops.name: seq.key_float
ops.summary: Key a float property of an actor or component: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], interp "auto" (smooth,
ops.doc:
Key a float property of an actor or component: keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], interp "auto" (smooth,
eased at held ends), "linear" or "constant" (stepped). `prop` is the C++ name or a path into structs, either
spelling: "Intensity", "Temperature", "FocusSettings.ManualFocusDistance" (CameraComponent), "CurrentAperture",
"Settings.AutoExposureBias" (a PostProcessVolume actor: set its override flag once with look.post), "FogDensity".
`component` by name or class ("CameraComponent", "LightComponent0"); "" = the actor if it has the property, else
its root component (a light's). `double` for a double property (a UE5 large-world value). Replaces only this
property's track on that binding; the keys hold before the first and after the last.

ops.name: seq.key_material
ops.summary: Key a material parameter on a mesh component's material slot (the material there must be an instance or
ops.doc:
Key a material parameter on a mesh component's material slot (the material there must be an instance or
material with that parameter): keys [[frame, value(, interp)], ...], a float for a scalar parameter or
[r, g, b(, a)] (linear) for a vector one. `slot` is its index or name ("M_Sheer"); `component` "" = the actor's
first mesh component. Replaces only that parameter's keys in the slot's track; other parameters keep theirs.

ops.name: seq.key_transform
ops.summary: Animate an actor in a sequence: keys are [frame, [x, y, z], {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} | [x, y, z] to look at]
ops.doc:
Animate an actor in a sequence: keys are [frame, [x, y, z], {"pitch", "yaw", "roll"} | [x, y, z] to look at]
with an optional 4th element, the interpolation leaving that key: "auto" (smooth, eases at held ends), "linear"
or "constant" (hold until the next key, a jump cut). `interp` is the default. Replaces the actor's transform
track (and only that), keeping the actor's scale; yaw is keyed as given, so unwrap it yourself across +-180.

ops.name: seq.key_visible

ops.doc:

first key holds before it. Overrides the level's hidden state while the sequence is open or playing (a

ops.doc:
Play a sequence frame by frame across editor ticks (so animation and rigs settle) and record bones' world
transforms, each [x, y, z, axis_x(3), axis_y(3), axis_z(3)], `camera`'s location, and `target`'s (see

ops.name: shot.apply
ops.summary: Shoot a shot list into its sequence: make or move each shot's camera (framed by the solver, the coverage or an
ops.doc:
Shoot a shot list into its sequence: make or move each shot's camera (framed by the solver, the coverage or an
explicit placement), key its moves, focal length and focus, and replace the sequence's camera cuts. Converges:
the same spec again changes nothing (force=True rewrites anyway); cameras the previous spec made that this one
drops are removed. A multi-tick job: the keys and cuts go in one batched seq.apply when WP8's core is there.

Returns: shot.plan's result plus {"changed", "cameras": {label: {"created", "keys"}}, "removed", "write"}.
Example: film-ue op shot.apply spec=@films/demo/shots/scene1.yaml

ops.name: shot.check
ops.summary: Check a sequence's edit numerically: every shot's frame (cam.check: QA's framing plus focus, safe areas,
ops.doc:
Check a sequence's edit numerically: every shot's frame (cam.check: QA's framing plus focus, safe areas,
dutch) at its start (or "middle"), and every cut (180-degree line, 30-degree rule). Scrubs the sequence: a
multi-tick job.

Returns: {"pass", "issues", "shots": [{"camera", "start", "end", "size"}]}.
Example: film-ue op shot.check sequence=/Game/Films/demo/Seq_Scene1 'subjects=["Host","Guest"]'

ops.doc:

ops.name: shot.plan
ops.summary: Resolve a shot list against the level without changing anything: each shot's camera, frames, size, lens,
ops.doc:
Resolve a shot list against the level without changing anything: each shot's camera, frames, size, lens,
keys, the cuts, and every framing/cut issue. The dry run of shot.apply.

Args: spec: a kind "shot" spec (docs/unreal/camera.md; schema tools/filmtools/unreal/schemas/shot.schema.json).
Returns: {"sequence", "range", "cuts", "shots": [...], "issues": [...], "coverage", "spec_hash",
"up_to_date": whether the sequence already holds this exact spec}.
Example: film-ue op shot.plan spec=@films/demo/shots/scene1.yaml

A previz contact sheet of a sequence's edit: per shot 1 (its middle) or 3 (start, middle, end) stills

ops.name: view.camera
ops.summary: Where things land in a camera's frame, without rendering: the camera as numbers, and world points or actors'
ops.doc:
Where things land in a camera's frame, without rendering: the camera as numbers, and world points or actors'
bounds projected to frame fractions (u right, v down, 0..1).

Args: camera: label ("" + sequence/frame: the cut's camera; the sequence is scrubbed there). points: {name:
[x,y,z]}. actors: labels (their bounds' screen boxes). width_px/height_px: the output aspect.
Returns: {"camera": {name, loc, rot, fov, aspect, focal?, sensor_width?}, "points": {name: {u, v, depth_cm,
in_frame}}, "actors": {label: {box, in_frame, area}}, "aspect_mismatch"?}.
Example: film-ue op view.camera camera=CamA 'actors=["Ada","Chair"]'

ops.name: view.overlay
ops.summary: Draw composition guides, labelled boxes and points on a copy of an image (no PIL needed).
ops.doc:
Draw composition guides, labelled boxes and points on a copy of an image (no PIL needed).

Args: image: PNG path. out: where the annotated copy goes. guides: any of thirds, safe (action 93% / title 90%),
center, golden, headroom, grid:4x3, aspect:2.39 (masks to that aspect). boxes: [{"box": [x0,y0,x1,y1] (0..1),
"label", "color": ok|info|warn|fail|[r,g,b]}]. points: [{"at": [x,y], "label"}]. caption: a text bar along the
bottom. width_px: shrink first (0 keeps the size).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op view.overlay image=/tmp/qa/a.png out=/tmp/qa/a_g.png 'guides=["thirds","safe"]'

ops.name: view.sheet
ops.summary: A contact sheet from PNG files on the box: a grid of labelled frames in one image.
ops.doc:
A contact sheet from PNG files on the box: a grid of labelled frames in one image.

Args: images: paths. out: the sheet's PNG path. labels: one per image (default the file names). cols: 0 picks a
near-square grid. cell_width_px: each frame's width. title: a bar on top. statuses: ok|info|warn|fail per image
(a coloured border).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "cells", "changed": true}.
Example: film-ue op view.sheet 'images=["/tmp/a.png","/tmp/b.png"]' out=/tmp/sheet.png title=compare

ops.name: view.still
ops.summary: A PNG of what a camera sees, with no viewport.
ops.doc:
A PNG of what a camera sees, with no viewport.

Args: out: the PNG path on the box. camera: a camera actor label; "" with `sequence`+`frame` takes the camera
the cut shows at that frame; "" with `loc`/`look_at` [x,y,z] cm makes an ad-hoc camera (`fov_deg`, default 40).
sequence/frame: scrub the sequence there first (frames at its display rate). width_px/height_px: output size.
mode: "capture" (a scene capture: fast, ~0.1-1 s, no motion blur/DoF accumulation), "mrq" (Movie Render Queue
through render.frames: the final look, slower; needs sequence+frame and `level`), "viewport" (look.still's
high-res screenshot). warmup: captures before the kept one (temporal AA, Lumen). settle_ticks: editor ticks after
a scrub. hide: actor labels left out. guides: overlay guides drawn on a copy saved as <out>.guides.png
("thirds", "safe", ...). rt_format: capture mode's render target format (advanced; default RTF_RGBA8, the
selftest compares it with RTF_RGBA8_SRGB against a viewport still).
Returns: {"path", "width", "height", "camera", "mode", "frame", "camera_info": {loc, rot, fov, aspect},
"guides_path"?}. A multi-tick job.
Example: film-ue op view.still out=/tmp/qa/a.png camera=CamA width_px=960 height_px=540

ops.name: view.stills
ops.summary: Stills through a sequence's edit and a contact sheet of them: the whole cut in one picture.
ops.doc:
Stills through a sequence's edit and a contact sheet of them: the whole cut in one picture.

Args: sequence: the level sequence path. out_dir: where {frame:05d}.png and sheet.png go. frames: the frames to
take; None takes `per_shot` per camera cut (first, middle(s), last). camera: force one camera ("" follows the
cut). width_px/height_px/mode/warmup/settle_ticks: as view.still. sheet: also write sheet.png with each frame
labelled "frame camera". guides: drawn on the sheet's cells.
Returns: {"frames": [{"frame", "camera", "path"}], "sheet": path|None, "width", "height"}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op view.stills sequence=/Game/Seq/S010 out_dir=/tmp/qa/s010 per_shot=2

ops.name: view.turntable
ops.summary: Stills of an actor from all around (a character, a prop, a garment) and a contact sheet of them.
ops.doc:
Stills of an actor from all around (a character, a prop, a garment) and a contact sheet of them.

Args: target: actor label. out_dir: where view_<yaw>.png and sheet.png go. views: how many, evenly around.
elevation_deg: the cameras' height angle above the target's centre. distance_cm: 0 frames the bounds with a
margin. fov_deg: horizontal. isolate: draw only the target (no set; lights still light it). start_yaw_deg: the
first view's direction from the target (0 = from +X, looking back at it).
Returns: {"views": [{"yaw", "path", "camera": {loc, rot, fov}}], "sheet", "center", "distance_cm"}. Multi-tick.
Example: film-ue op view.turntable target=Ada out_dir=/tmp/qa/ada views=8 isolate=true
